documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
New patient, 42F, here to establish primary care. Prior PCP retired; records requested.

Background: remote T12 spinal cord injury with neurogenic bladder. Manages her bladder with clean intermittent self-catheterization, latex-free catheters, about every 4-6 hours. Followed by an outside urology group once a year or so. Long history of bladder infections; she says cultures usually come back Proteus. Urology has told her the Proteus is chronic colonization and not to be treated unless she is symptomatic. Takes oxybutynin for bladder spasm/leakage, methenamine for prevention, and docusate for her bowel program. Nothing acute today.

PMH: neurogenic bladder after T12 SCI; recurrent UTIs; chronic Proteus mirabilis bacteriuria.
PSH: appendectomy 2005.
Meds: oxybutynin 5 mg TID, methenamine hippurate 1 g BID, docusate 100 mg BID.
Allergies: TMP-SMX (Stevens-Johnson syndrome). LATEX — needs latex-free gloves and supplies.
FH: mother has had kidney stones many times; father with hypertension.
SH: data analyst, works remotely. Quit smoking 2015, about 10 pack-years. Does not drink.

ROS: no fever, no flank pain, no hematuria. Bowel program working. Mood good.

Exam: NAD, pleasant. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally. Abdomen soft, nontender, healed RLQ scar. No CVA tenderness. Skin intact over sacrum and heels, no pressure areas. Neuro: upper extremities strength and sensation normal; lower-extremity findings at her known baseline from the cord injury.

A/P:
1. Neurogenic bladder, remote T12 SCI — stable on CIC. Continue oxybutynin, methenamine. Will get urology notes. Latex allergy flagged in chart.
2. Recurrent UTI / chronic Proteus bacteriuria — agree with urology, no urine testing unless symptomatic. Avoid TMP-SMX (SJS). Reviewed red flags: fever, flank pain, new spasm or autonomic symptoms -> call same day.
3. Former smoker, 10 pack-years — no lung screening indicated.
4. Health maintenance: CMP, CBC, lipids, one-time hep C and HIV today. Asked for prior Pap and mammogram reports. Flu and COVID next month at nurse visit.

RTC 1 year for physical, sooner as needed. Text or call anytime.

documents.title: Acute Visit — UTI symptoms
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 44F with neurogenic bladder on CIC, chronic Proteus colonization. 2 days of burning with catheterization, cloudy foul urine. No fever or chills, no flank pain, no increase in spasms. Says this is her typical infection.
O: afebrile, vitals reviewed and normal. Abdomen soft, mild suprapubic tenderness, no CVA tenderness.
UA in office: cloudy, pH 7.5, LE 2+, nitrite +, WBC 40/hpf, RBC 3/hpf. Culture sent.
A/P: symptomatic lower UTI, likely her usual Proteus. TMP-SMX contraindicated (SJS) and Proteus is intrinsically resistant to nitrofurantoin, so cephalexin 500 mg BID x 7 days. Will adjust to culture. Fluids, continue CIC schedule. Call for fever or flank pain.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional emergency department. Date of visit 06/17/2025. Received by fax.

CC: R flank pain, burning x2 days.
HPI: 45 y/o F, neurogenic bladder from T12 SCI on intermittent cath. Two days of right-sided flank pain, steady, moving down into the groin. Burning with urination, constant urge, getting only small volumes of cloudy urine. No fever. No nausea or vomiting.
PMH: neurogenic bladder, recurrent UTIs, chronic Proteus bacteriuria. PSH: appendectomy.
Home meds: oxybutynin, methenamine, docusate.
Allergies: TMP-SMX (SJS), LATEX.
SH: former smoker, no EtOH. FH: mother with kidney stones.

Exam: uncomfortable, shifting in bed. Afebrile. Right CVA tenderness. Abdomen soft, no peritoneal signs.
UA: pH 8.5, pyuria, crystals seen on microscopy. Gram stain of urine: no organisms.

MDM: presentation consistent with right renal colic in a patient with a family history of stones. No signs of infection on stain, afebrile. Pain controlled.
Dx: urolithiasis / right renal colic.
Disposition: home. Tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily, acetaminophen 1 g q6h prn. Strain urine. Follow up with urology and PCP this week. Return for fever, vomiting, uncontrolled pain.

documents.title: Went to the ER last night
documents.author: patient
documents.body: FYI I was in the ER last night with right side pain — they think a kidney stone. My mom has had these forever so I guess it was my turn. They gave me tamsulosin and said strain my urine. Pain is better this morning. Do you need to see me?

documents.title: Re: Went to the ER last night
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sorry you went through that. Their record just came in. Yes, let's see you next Tuesday and check kidney function. Keep the tamsulosin going and strain everything. Fever, vomiting or pain you can't control = back to the ED or call me directly. I'll let your urologist's office know too.

Regional emergency department, visit 10/19/2025. Received electronically.

CC: fever, R flank pain, burning.
HPI: 45F with neurogenic bladder (T12 SCI), recurrent UTIs and known Proteus colonization, with an indwelling urethral catheter for the past several weeks. Presents with fever, right flank pain and dysuria. Seen here in June for right renal colic.
Meds: oxybutynin, methenamine, tamsulosin, docusate. Allergies: TMP-SMX (SJS), latex.

Triage: T 38.6 C, HR 102, BP 124/76, RR 18, SpO2 98% RA.
Exam: ill-appearing but nontoxic. Right CVA tenderness. Abdomen soft. Catheter in place, cloudy urine in bag.
UA: alkaline (pH 8.5); microscopy with rectangular prism-shaped crystals. Urine culture sent from the new catheter.
KUB: radiopaque calculus over the right renal shadow.

Course: ceftriaxone 1 g IV. Catheter exchanged for a new latex-free catheter. Defervesced, tolerating PO.
Dx: catheter-associated UTI; right renal calculus.
Dispo: home on ciprofloxacin 500 mg BID x 7 days (TMP-SMX allergy). Urology follow-up for the stone. PCP within a week. Return for rigors, vomiting, worsening pain.

documents.title: Post-ED call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called after ED visit Sunday. ED culture resulted this morning: Proteus mirabilis, sensitive to cipro. Pt on day 3 of ciprofloxacin, no fever since Sunday night, flank pain easing. Catheter draining well. Booked with PCP 10/28. Advised to call if fever returns.

documents.title: Urology discharge summary
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Regional hospital, urology service. Admitted 02/14/2026, discharged 02/18/2026.

Reason for admission: 46-year-old woman with neurogenic bladder after T12 spinal cord injury on an indwelling catheter, recurrent UTIs with Proteus mirabilis, seen in the ED in June and October 2025, admitted with two weeks of right flank pain and fevers on and off, with burning and urgency.

Allergies: trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (Stevens-Johnson syndrome); latex — latex-free precautions.
Home medications: oxybutynin 5 mg TID, methenamine hippurate 1 g BID, tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily, docusate 100 mg BID.

On admission: T 38.3 C. Right CVA tenderness. WBC 12,000. UA pH 8.0, leukocyte esterase and nitrite positive, numerous WBCs. Creatinine 1.2 (baseline 0.9), BUN 18. Non-contrast CT: large staghorn calculus in the right renal pelvis.

Hospital course: started on IV ceftriaxone 1 g daily. Urine culture grew Proteus mirabilis sensitive to ceftriaxone and ciprofloxacin. Fevers resolved by day 2. Catheter exchanged. Creatinine 1.0 at discharge. Discussed definitive management of the staghorn stone: right percutaneous nephrolithotomy once the infection is treated.

Discharge diagnoses: right staghorn calculus; complicated UTI with Proteus mirabilis; neurogenic bladder.
Discharge medications: ciprofloxacin 500 mg BID to finish a 14-day course; home medications unchanged.
Follow-up: PCP in 1 week; urology will call with a surgery date.

documents.title: In the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Writing from a hospital bed — admitted Saturday with fever and the right side again. The CT shows a big stone filling the kidney. They're talking surgery through the back. Fever is gone today. Just wanted you to know.

documents.title: Re: In the hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for telling me, and glad the fever's down. That surgery (PCNL) is the standard way to clear a large stone like this. I'll watch for the discharge summary — let's see you about a week after you get home.

documents.title: Post-discharge Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Admitted 2/14-2/18 to urology: febrile Proteus UTI with a large right staghorn calculus on CT. WBC 12K, Cr 1.2 on admission, 1.0 at discharge. IV ceftriaxone then cipro to complete 14 days. PCNL planned.

Today: day 10 of antibiotics. Afebrile since the 15th. Mild right-sided ache, no rigors. Catheter draining. Eating normally.
Meds reconciled: oxybutynin 5 TID, methenamine 1 g BID, tamsulosin 0.4 daily, docusate 100 BID, cipro 500 BID through 2/27.
Exam: afebrile, well. Faint R CVA tenderness. Abdomen soft.

A/P:
1. Right staghorn calculus with Proteus infection — finishing cipro. Urology to schedule PCNL. Will do preop eval here when the date is set.
2. Creatinine 1.0 today, near baseline.
3. Neurogenic bladder on indwelling catheter — unchanged.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Preoperative Evaluation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Preop for right percutaneous nephrolithotomy, scheduled 3/24 with urology.

Finished cipro 2/27. No fever since. Ache in the right flank comes and goes. No chest pain, no dyspnea, good functional capacity for her baseline. No prior anesthesia problems (appendectomy 2005). Former smoker, quit 2015.
Meds: oxybutynin, methenamine, tamsulosin, docusate. No anticoagulants or antiplatelets.
Allergies: TMP-SMX — SJS. LATEX — needs latex-free OR.

Exam: afebrile, vitals normal. Airway unremarkable. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Mild R CVA tenderness. Skin intact over pressure points.
ECG: normal sinus rhythm. CBC, BMP drawn.

Assessment: low-risk patient for an intermediate-risk procedure. No further cardiac or pulmonary testing needed. Medically acceptable to proceed.
Recommendations to surgical team: latex-free environment; no TMP-SMX; recent culture Proteus mirabilis sensitive to ceftriaxone and cipro for perioperative prophylaxis planning; usual bowel program. Letter faxed.

documents.author: MA

documents.title: Right percutaneous nephrolithotomy
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Regional hospital, urology. Date of surgery 03/24/2026. Received 03/26.

Preoperative and postoperative diagnosis: right staghorn calculus.
Procedure: right percutaneous nephrolithotomy; antegrade right ureteral stent placement.
Anesthesia: general. Latex-free room. Prophylaxis per culture (ceftriaxone).
Findings: large branched calculus filling the right renal pelvis, removed with ultrasonic lithotripsy and graspers; fragments sent for analysis. No visible residual stone on final nephroscopy and fluoroscopy. A double-J ureteral stent placed antegrade. No nephrostomy tube left.
EBL minimal. No complications. Urethral catheter exchanged.
Disposition: observed overnight, discharged 03/25 afebrile. Stent removal in about 2 weeks; CT to confirm stone clearance in 6-8 weeks.

Outside urology group. Visit 05/12/2026.

Six weeks after right PCNL for a struvite staghorn. Feels well, no fevers. Today's non-contrast CT shows no residual stone and no hydronephrosis.

Allergies: TMP-SMX (SJS), latex.
Medications: oxybutynin 5 mg TID, methenamine hippurate 1 g BID, tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily, docusate 100 mg BID.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Catch-up after the stone course. 46F.

Recap: right struvite staghorn (Proteus), admission in Feb, right PCNL 3/24, stent out 4/7, CT 5/12 stone-free. Indwelling catheter removed 5/12; back on CIC q4-6h with latex-free catheters, supplies reauthorized. No fevers or flank pain since. Urine clear. Urology in November with a KUB.
Meds: oxybutynin 5 TID, methenamine 1 g BID, tamsulosin 0.4 daily, docusate 100 BID. Allergies: TMP-SMX (SJS), latex.

Exam: well, vitals normal. Heart RRR, lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Right flank puncture site well healed. No CVA tenderness. Skin intact over sacrum. LE neuro at baseline. Pelvic exam with latex-free speculum, normal cervix; Pap/HPV collected.

A/P:
1. Kidney stone, right, s/p PCNL, stone-free. Creatinine today. Urology surveillance.
2. Neurogenic bladder, back to CIC. Continue regimen.
3. Recurrent UTI/chronic Proteus: no treatment unless symptomatic; call early with fever.
4. HM: Pap/HPV today (last 2021). FIT due — kit given. Mammogram 1/2026. Physical booked 9/22, flu and COVID then.
